sections.title: Basic Concept of One Word Substitution
sections.content: In One Word Substitution, a long sentence or idea is expressed using a single precise word. In competitive exams, you have to identify the correct word for a given phrase. Step 1: Understand the main meaning of the phrase. Step 2: Identify the commonly used single word for it. Step 3: Confirm the meaning using the root or suffix of the word.

sections.title: Phobias (Fears)
sections.content: Phobia means an abnormal fear of a specific thing. Step 1: Identify the object or situation causing the fear. Step 2: Check whether the word ends with 'phobia'. Step 3: Identify the object of fear using the root word. Example: Hydrophobia = fear of water, Claustrophobia = fear of closed spaces.

sections.title: Cides (Killings)
sections.content: Cide means killing or the act of killing. Step 1: Identify who or what is being killed. Step 2: Check if the word ends with 'cide'. Step 3: Identify the relationship using the root word. Example: Patricide = killing of one's father, Infanticide = killing of an infant, Regicide = killing of a king.

sections.title: Specialists and Ologies
sections.content: Ology means the study of a subject, and ologist refers to a specialist in that subject. Step 1: Identify the subject. Step 2: Check whether the word contains 'ology' or 'ologist'. Step 3: Understand the subject using the root word. Example: Cardiologist = heart specialist, Ornithology = study of birds, Pathology = study of diseases.

sections.title: Basic Personality Types
sections.content: Some words describe types of personality or thinking. Step 1: Understand the behavior of the person. Step 2: Identify the related personality word. Step 3: Remember the general meaning of the word. Example: Optimist = a person with positive thinking, Pessimist = a person with negative thinking, Introvert = a person who speaks less or prefers solitude, Altruist = a person who works for the welfare of others.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Choosing a word without understanding the root meaning. 2. Confusing similar-looking words. 3. Ignoring suffixes like phobia, cide, and ology.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Understanding suffixes and root meanings is very helpful in One Word Substitution. Phobia indicates fear, Cide indicates killing, Ology indicates study, and personality words describe a person's nature.

tricks.title: Phobia Suffix Trick
tricks.explanation: Any word ending with 'phobia' represents a fear.

tricks.title: Ology Study Trick
tricks.explanation: 'Ology' means the study of a subject.

tricks.title: Ologist Expert Trick
tricks.explanation: 'Ologist' refers to a specialist in that subject.

tricks.title: Personality Word Memory
tricks.explanation: Remember words based on a person's nature or behavior.

tricks.title: Root Meaning Trick
tricks.explanation: Try to understand the meaning of a word using its root.

tricks.title: Opposite Personality Pair
tricks.explanation: Some personality words are easier to remember in pairs.

tricks.title: Elimination Method
tricks.explanation: If you cannot recall the correct word immediately, eliminate incorrect options.
tricks.example: If the phrase refers to fear, choose the word ending with 'phobia'.
